study: studies/measurement/stability-selection (stability.py) -- stability selection and the edge error curve, Paper II F3
note: STABILITY SELECTION (complementary pairs, B = 50, top-q per half with q set so the Meinshausen-Buhlmann bound at tau 0.75 is 1) ON THE RELIABILITY STUDY'S DROP, pre-registered at 50bef7e. Floors pass: kappa_bar's floor world reproduced exactly (2,507 edges, precision 0.0750); a sparse planted graph is recovered at precision 0.971 with V 0.7 under a bound of 0.997; planted decoy pairs break the bound visibly (V 4.8 at the smallest decoy). BOUND HONESTY, N 32,000, density 0.10, tau 0.75, 20 worlds: kappa_bar's world 1.20 [0.70, 1.75] vs 0.997 (VIOLATED, marginal); order-independent session noise 0.90 (HONEST); curriculum-ordered 0.95 vs 0.986 (HONEST); pre-registered verdict NOT SUPPORTED: THE BOUND HOLDS UNDER CURRICULUM ORDER. Curriculum order does make false edges more stable (top-10 false pi 0.548 vs 0.339) and breaks the bound decisively at tau 0.60 (3.45 vs 2.46). ERROR CURVE of the adopted rule (500 -> 32,000 learners, kappa_bar's world): precision 0.085 -> 0.074 (flat), sensitivity 0.372 -> 0.949, specificity 0.784 -> 0.365: more learners do not buy accuracy. The stability-selected set is about 95% precise at sensitivity 0.15. REAL: XES3G5M 10 (9 on a second run) edges stable at tau 0.75 of 32,362 candidates, EdNet 0 of 15,138; deranged nulls select 0 on both (BOUND HONEST UNDER THE DERANGED NULL), but in simulation the deranged null cannot see ability or session artefacts, and EdNet's deranged cells are 0.43x the real ones. A5 is a repeatability gate and nothing here changes its standing. Moves nothing.
